sources.entry: M-Courtyard - Desktop app for fine-tuning LLMs on Apple Silicon Macs with zero code. Import documents, generate training datasets with AI, LoRA fine-tune, test, and export to Ollama — entirely offline.

summary.one_liner: A macOS desktop app that guides users through preparing documents into datasets, LoRA fine-tuning of local LLMs on Apple Silicon via MLX, testing, and exporting to Ollama or MLX formats, all without writing code.
summary.what_it_does: M-Courtyard is a desktop app for macOS (Apple Silicon) that walks users through a four-step pipeline: importing data, generating datasets, fine-tuning, and exporting. It imports .txt, .pdf, and .docx files by drag and drop, cleans and chunks them, and builds instruction-style datasets such as Knowledge Q&A, Style Imitation, or Instruction Training. Dataset generation can use local Ollama or LM Studio models, or a built-in rules mode that needs no external runtime. Training uses LoRA via mlx-lm, with presets (Quick, Standard, Thorough) and live loss charts and ETA. Users can chat with the resulting adapter in the app, then export it by merging and quantizing (Q4/Q8/F16) to Ollama, or as fused MLX models for mlx-lm.server or LM Studio. The README says the app's Python and mlx-lm environment is set up automatically via uv.
use_cases: fine-tune an LLM on private company documents
turn PDFs and Word files into training datasets
train a personal writing-style model offline
export a custom model to Ollama without coding
run LoRA fine-tuning on a Mac without CUDA
generate instruction datasets from local documents
how_to_run: Download the latest .dmg from the Releases page and drag M-Courtyard.app to Applications
Build from source: git clone the repo and cd m-courtyard/app
notable: Zero-code pipeline from raw PDF/DOCX files to a fine-tuned model that can be exported
Fully local: the README says no data leaves the machine
Built-in rules mode generates datasets with no Ollama or LM Studio installed
Sets AGX_RELAX_CDM_CTXSTORE_TIMEOUT=1 for training subprocesses to work around a macOS Tahoe Metal watchdog issue
One-click export to Ollama (merge and quantize) and MLX export for LM Studio
caveats: Requires macOS 14+ and Apple Silicon (M1 through M4); not for Intel Macs or other platforms
16 GB+ RAM recommended for 7B/8B models; 8 GB only suits small models (1.5B/3B)
The app is not code-signed, so macOS needs a quarantine-removal command to launch it
Ollama and LM Studio are optional; Ollama is needed for Ollama dataset generation and Ollama export
Source build requires Node.js 18+, pnpm, the Rust toolchain, and Xcode Command Line Tools
Commercial use or different license terms require contacting the author
